chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Abān ibn Taghlib, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī was the last of those who remained from the companions of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله, and he was a man devoted to us, Ahl al-Bayt. He would sit in the Masjid of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله, wrapped in a black turban, and he would call out: “O splitter of knowledge, O splitter of knowledge.”

The people of al-Madīnah used to say, “Jābir is raving.” But he would say, “No, by Allah, I am not raving. Rather, I heard Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله say: ‘You will meet a man from me whose name is my name and whose qualities are my qualities; he will split open knowledge completely.’ That is what has led me to what I am saying.”

He said: While Jābir was walking one day in one of the streets of al-Madīnah, he passed along a way where there was a school in which Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī was present. When he looked at him, he said, “O boy, come forward.” So he came forward. Then he said to him, “Turn back.” So he turned back. Then he said, “These are the qualities of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله. By the One in whose hand is my soul, O boy, what is your name?” He said, “My name is Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn.” Then he came to him, kissing his head and saying, “May my father and mother be sacrificed for you; your forefather Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله conveys salām to you and said that.”

He said: Then Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn returned to his father while alarmed, and informed him of the matter. He said to him, “My son, has Jābir done this?” He said, “Yes.” He said, “Stay in your house, my son.” Thereafter Jābir would come to him at the two ends of the day, and the people of al-Madīnah would say, “How astonishing about Jābir! He comes to this boy at the two ends of the day, while he is the last remaining of the companions of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله.”

It was not long before ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام passed away. Then Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī would come to him out of honoring his companionship with Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله. He said: Then he عليه السلام sat and narrated to them from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, so the people of al-Madīnah said, “We have not seen anyone more daring than this.” When he saw what they were saying, he narrated to them from Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله, so the people of al-Madīnah said, “We have never seen anyone more untruthful than this, narrating to us from one whom he did not see.” When he saw what they were saying, he narrated to them from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh. Then they affirmed him, and Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh used to come to him and learn from him.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: the Household of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله

key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: al-Madīnah, where these events took place

ai.seo_question: How did Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh recognize Imam Muḥammad al-Bāqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This narration describes the recognition of Imam Muḥammad al-Bāqir عليه السلام by Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī based on a prior statement of Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله. It highlights the special knowledge of the Imam, the devotion of Jābir to Ahl al-Bayt, and the eventual public acknowledgment of the Imam’s authority in transmitting divine and Prophetic knowledge.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Aban Bin Taghlub, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Jabir Bin Abdullah Al-Ansary was the last ones to remain, from the companions of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and he was a man who had cut himself off to us<sup>asws</sup>, the People<sup>asws</sup> of the Household, and he was sitting in the Masjid of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and he was turbaned with a black turban, and he was calling out, ‘يَا بَاقِرَ الْعِلْمِ يَا بَاقِرَ الْعِلْم’ ‘O expounder of the knowledge! O expounder of the knowledge!

And it was so that the people of Al-Medina were saying, ‘Jabir is hallucinating’. So he was saying, ‘No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I am not hallucinating. But, I heard Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> saying: ‘You (Jabir) would be coming across a man from me<sup>saww</sup>, his<sup>asws</sup> name would be my<sup>saww</sup> name, and his<sup>asws</sup> mannerisms would be my<sup>saww</sup> mannerisms. He<sup>asws</sup> would expound the knowledge with an expansion’. So that is what is calling me to what I am saying’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So while Jabir was walking around one day in one of the streets of Al-Median, when some scribes passed by in that street, among whom was Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>. So when he looked at him<sup>asws</sup>, he said, ‘O boy<sup>asws</sup>! Come!’ So, he<sup>asws</sup> came. Then he said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! The mannerisms of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, by the One<sup>azwj</sup> in Whose Hand is my soul! O boy<sup>asws</sup>! What is your<sup>asws</sup> name?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> name is Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>’. So he went faced him<sup>asws</sup>, and kissed his<sup>asws</sup> head and he was saying, ‘By my father and my mother be (sacrificed) for you<sup>asws</sup>! Your<sup>asws</sup> father Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> conveys the greetings to you<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>saww</sup> was saying (all) that’.

Heasws said: ‘So Muhammadasws Bin Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws returned to hisasws fatherasws, and heasws was alarmed, So, heasws informed himasws of the news. So, heasws said to himasws: ‘O myasws sonasws, and Jabir did it?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’. Heasws said: ‘Necessitated yourasws house (stay at home), O myasws son!’ So Jabir used to come to himasws at both ends of the day, and the people of Al-Medina were saying, ‘O how strange of Jabir to come to this boyasws at both ends of the day, and he is the last one to remain from the companions of Rasool-Allahsaww’.

It was not long before Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> passed away (martyred), and Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> used to go to him (Jabir Bin Abdullah) upon the aspect of the honour of his companionship to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. He<sup>asws</sup> would sit and narrate to them (directly) from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High. The people of Al-Medina would say, ‘We have not seen anyone so audacious than this one’. 
When he<sup>asws</sup> saw what they were saying, he<sup>asws</sup> narrated to them (directly) from Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. So, the people of Al-Medina said, ‘We have not seen anyone at all more lying than this one (Nouzobillah), narrating to us from the one<sup>saww</sup> he<sup>asws</sup> has not even seen. When he<sup>asws</sup> saw what they were saying, he<sup>asws</sup> narrated to them from Jabir Bin Abdullah. (In that way) they ratified him<sup>asws</sup>, and it was so that Jabir Bin Abdullah used to come to him<sup>asws</sup>, to learn from him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: Muhammad ibn al-Hassan has narrated from ‘Abdallah ibn Ahmad has narrated a similar hadith.
